name: Deep wall return, walk in, soft block
summary: Alone at a wall, hit a deep, high return above a tape line, walk in two to three steps and play the rebound back softly just above the net line, as the receiving side does after its return.
setup: Tape two lines on the wall: one about 0.9 m above the floor (the net) and one about 1.5 m (a deep, high return), and stand about 6 m from the wall
Toss the ball against the wall so it rebounds and bounces once in front of you, like a serve coming in
Return it off the bounce with a smooth stroke above the 1.5 m line, then walk two to three steps forward and stop balanced before the rebound reaches you
Let the rebound bounce, then play it back softly so it hits the wall between the two lines: this is the shot after the return. Catch the next rebound, walk back and repeat. Sets of 10 patterns
success_criterion: In each of 3 sets of 10 patterns, at least 7 patterns have the return above the 1.5 m line and the soft shot between the two lines
safety_notes: Soft to medium pace: the return is deep and high, never a drive at the wall. Walk forward, never sprint, and never backpedal for a rebound; let it go. Clear the floor of loose balls between sets. Stop if dizzy or in pain.
coach_rationale: (judgment) Rallies won when receiving (AN-02) are mostly lost to the serving side's attack on a short return or on the shot after it. A deep, high return buys the time to move in, and a soft shot from a balanced stop keeps the next ball unattackable; one solo wall pattern trains both with no partner or court.
